━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━

📊 SWING TRADING SETUP: The 3-Day Breakout Pattern

Swing trading captures medium-term moves over 2-10 days. Today we focus on a reliable setup: the 3-day consolidation breakout.

What to look for:
- Stock trades in tight range for 3 consecutive days
- Range should be within 2-3 percent of previous close
- Volume decreases each day (compression phase)
- Price sits near resistance or support level

Real example: Tech stocks after Fed announcements often consolidate before making directional moves. Watch how NVDA consolidated July 21-23 before breaking to new highs on July 24.

Entry trigger:
- Wait for breakout candle with volume 50 percent above average
- Enter on break of day 3 high (for longs) or low (for shorts)
- Place stop below the 3-day range low (longs) or above high (shorts)

Target: Measure the prior swing move and project same distance from breakout point.

PRO TIP: Best swing setups occur after earnings releases when uncertainty clears and new trends emerge. Avoid entering during consolidation - patience pays.

━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━

💼 EARNINGS SEASON: Reading Between The Lines

We are in peak Q2 2026 earnings season. Over 60 percent of S&P 500 companies report in the next two weeks.

What moves stocks:
- Not just the earnings beat or miss
- Forward guidance matters 3x more than past results
- Management tone on conference calls reveals true picture

Key sectors reporting this week:
- Mega-cap tech (cloud growth rates critical)
- Regional banks (loan quality under scrutiny)
- Consumer discretionary (spending trends matter)

How to trade earnings:
- Avoid holding through announcement if you are risk-averse
- IV crush destroys option value post-earnings
- Best plays: wait 24 hours, trade the trend confirmation

Example: When MSFT beat estimates July 25 but guided lower on Azure growth, stock dropped 4 percent despite earnings beat. Guidance trumps results every time.

Watch for sector rotation signals. If financials guide strong while tech guides weak, money flows shift quickly.

SMART MONEY RULE: Institutions position 2-3 days before earnings based on channel checks and supply chain data. Unusual option activity often signals their positioning.

━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━

⚡ 3 DAILY TIPS FOR WEDNESDAY TRADING

TIP 1 - Fed Minutes Released Today
- FOMC minutes from July meeting published 2pm ET
- Focus on inflation language and rate cut timeline
- Expect volatility spike in bonds and dollar pairs
- Trade the reaction, not the anticipation

TIP 2 - Summer Volume Dynamics
- Average daily volume down 22 percent in late July
- Thinner volume means wider spreads and false breakouts
- Use limit orders, avoid market orders on illiquid names
- Reduce position sizes by 30-40 percent vs normal

TIP 3 - Sector Strength Scanner
- Healthcare showing relative strength last 5 sessions
- Energy lagging on demand concerns
- Rotation into defensive sectors suggests caution
- Follow the money flow, not the noise

━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━

🛡️ PORTFOLIO EXPOSURE: The 50-30-20 Framework

Risk management determines long-term survival. Portfolio exposure control is your first defense against major drawdowns.

The professional approach:
- 50 percent: Core positions (high conviction, proven setups)
- 30 percent: Opportunistic trades (swing trades, sector plays)
- 20 percent: Cash or hedges (dry powder for corrections)

Why this matters now:
Market sitting near all-time highs with elevated valuations. August historically volatile month ahead. Smart traders reduce exposure before trouble hits.

Exposure calculation:
Add up all position values divided by total account size. If you are over 80 percent invested during uncertain conditions, you are overexposed.

Correlation risk:
Holding 5 tech stocks is not diversification. When sector sells off, all positions drop together. True diversification means uncorrelated assets.

Real scenario: March 2026 correction saw accounts with 90 percent exposure drop 18 percent while those with 50-30-20 framework dropped only 9 percent. Position sizing matters more than stock selection.

Adjustment rules:
- Cut exposure by 20 percent when VIX rises above 20
- Raise cash after strong runs (take profits into strength)
- Never be fully invested - always keep buying power

PRO TIP: Your position size should reflect both conviction level and market environment. High conviction in uncertain markets still means smaller size than medium conviction in stable trends.
